nodes.name: One-step electrodeposition of RMNCL
nodes.procedure: First, 10 mmol Co(NO3)2·6H2O, 10 mmol Ni(CH3COO)2·4H2O, 1.8 mmol RuCl3, and 1.2 mmol MnCl2·4H2O were dissolved in 60 mL of deionized water. The solution was mixed using a magnetic stirrer and ultrasonication to homogenize it. The homogenized solution was then transferred into an electrolytic cell. Electrodeposition was carried out utilizing a standard three-electrode system. A carbon cloth (2×2 cm) was soaked under the liquid as the working electrode. The reference electrode used was the saturated calomel electrode (SCE), while the counter electrode was a carbon rod. The samples were subjected to cyclic voltammetry, with a potential scan of 0 to -1.8 V vs.SCE, scanning rate of 50 mVs^{-1}, and 40 scanning cycles. The resulting samples were washed with anhydrous ethanol and deionized water, then dried in a vacuum drying oven. The sample obtained was named Ru,Mn-NiCo LDH (denoted as RMNCL).

nodes.name: Phosphorization of RMNCL to RMNCP
nodes.procedure: The prepared precursor [RMNCL] and NaH2PO2·H2O (2 g) were placed in the center and upstream side of the tube furnace, respectively. They were heated to 350°C under an argon atmosphere at a ramp rate of 2°C/min and held for two hours to synthesize the phosphide nanoflowers. Once cooled, the samples were removed and named Ru,Mn-NiCoP (denoted as RMNCP).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images of RMNCL show nanosheets evenly cultivated on carbon cloth surface. RMNCP, RNCP and NCP demonstrate interconnected nanosheet configuration retained after phosphatization with increased nanoflower thickness.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning electron microscopy (SEM) was utilized to investigate the microscopic morphology of the synthesized electrocatalysts. Fig. S1 depicts the even surface of the carbon cloth. Following electrodeposition... SEM images (Fig. 1c, S4 and S5) of the prepared RMNCP, Ru doped NiCoP (RNCP) and NiCoP (NCP) demonstrate that the interconnected nanosheet configuration are effectively retained...

nodes.characterization_summary: RMNCP exhibits nanosheet structure with lattice stripe spacings of 0.351 nm (001 plane) and 0.242 nm (111 plane). Lattice spacing increases after Ru and Mn co-doping compared to undoped NiCoP, confirming lattice expansion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) was utilized to demonstrate the unique structure of the various samples. Fig. 1d also shows that RMNCP has a nanosheet structure. Additionally, the RMNCP (Fig. 1e) exhibits lattice stripe spacings of 0.351 and 0.242 nm, which correspond to its (001) and (111) planes, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM image of RMNCP confirms nanoflower structure assembled from nanosheets. Corresponding EDS shows uniform distribution of Ru, Mn, Ni, Co and P elements.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) image shown in Fig. 1h also confirms that the synthesized RMNCP has a nanoflower structure assembled from nanosheets... Moreover, the corresponding energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) images display a uniform distribution of Ru, Mn, Ni, Co and P elements.

nodes.characterization_summary: UPS spectra of NCP, RNCP and RMNCP show RMNCP valence band maximum Ev = 4.72 eV (higher than RNCP 4.65 eV, NCP 4.55 eV) with greater distance from Fermi level. Ecutoff increased by 0.9-1.02 eV vs RNCP/NCP, indicating decreased work function.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As displayed in Fig. 2a and S11, the valence band maximum (EV) of RMNCP is 4.72 eV, which is considerably higher than those of RNCP (4.65 eV) and NCP (4.55 eV), with a greater distance from the Fermi energy level (EF, set to 0 eV).

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution XPS of RMNCL, RNCL, NCL shows negatively shifted Co 2p and Ni 2p binding energies in RMNCL vs NCL. RMNCP shows Ruδ+ state, Mn2+ (641.77 eV)/Mn3+ (644.00 eV)/Mn4+ (646.70 eV), negative shifts in Ni/Co 2p peaks after Ru/Mn doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution XPS spectra of (b) Co 2p and (c) Ni 2p for NCL, RNCL and RMNCL. High-resolution XPS spectra of (d) Co 2p and (e) Ni 2p for NCP, RNCP and RMNCP. High-resolution XPS spectra of (f) P 2p, (g) C 1s, Ru 3d and (h) Mn 2p for RMNCP.

nodes.characterization_summary: RMNCP corresponds to NiCoP phase (PDF#71-2336). RMNCL corresponds to NiCo LDH phase (PDF#40-0216).
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis (Fig. S17) shows that RMNCP corresponds well to the NiCoP phase (PDF#71-2336) and RMNCL corresponds well to the NiCo LDH phase (PDF#40-0216).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge XANES of RMNCP located between Co foil and CoO, indicating Co valence 0 to +2. Ru K-edge shows distinctions from Ru foil and RuO2, confirming Ruδ+ state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co K-edge XANES spectra (Fig. 3a) reveal that the Co K-edge is located between metallic Co foil and CoO... Ru K-edge EXAFS spectra (Fig. 3d) unveil distinctions in the Ru K-edge of RMNCP compared to Ru foil and RuO2, indicating a slight positive valence state of Ru (Ruδ+).

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS shows Co-P peak at ~1.6Å and Co-Ni at ~2.4Å for RMNCP. Ru-P bond peak at ~1.7Å confirms dispersed Ru doping. WT-EXAFS confirms Co-P at 5.5Å⁻¹ and Ru-P at 5.6Å⁻¹ with no Ru-Ru signals.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The FT-EXAFS spectra (Fig. 3b) exhibit a distinct peak at ~1.6Å... suggesting association with Co-P... The Ru-P bond can be ascribed to the distinct peak (~1.7Å)... Co K-edge WT-EXAFS spectra (Fig. 3c) reveal a pronounced Co-P signal at 5.5Å⁻¹... In RMNCP, a strong WT Ru-P signal is only observed at ~5.6Å⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: RMNCP shows smallest semi-circular diameter in Nyquist plots, indicating lowest resistance and fastest electron transfer rate among samples.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The results of electrochemical impedance spectroscopy indicate that compared to other samples, RMNCP has a smaller semi-circular diameter and therefore has lower resistance.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV in non-Faraday region yields double layer capacitance Cdl = 41 mF/cm² for RMNCP (highest, >2x NCP), indicating largest electrochemically active surface area.
nodes.evidence_snippet: RMNCP exhibits the greatest Cdl value (ESCA = 41 mFcm⁻²) which is more than twice the Cdl value of NCP. This observation suggests that RMNCP possesses more substantial active sites...

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS tests before/after HER reaction show very few leached ions in solution for RMNCP.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Importantly, ICP-MS tests (Tables S1 and S2) before and after the reaction showed very few leached ions in solution, further validating these conclusions.
